text:
Ravi M: Quick sync: per-tenant fast-path idea to avoid noisy neighbor trips. Sketch: each tenant gets a tiny burst bucket (N tokens) that bypasses global breaker for tiny requests.
Noa: Sounds good. How tiny is tiny? We should define by token-count or latency budget. Small requests = < 200 tokens or < 50ms queuing.
Jules: Implementation note: fast-path should still decrement quota so accounting is consistent. Also make it configurable per tenant tier (free, standard, reserved).
Priya: I'm worried about abuse. Free tier could hammer the fast-path and starve others. Need a refill rate + short cooldown on abuse.
Ravi M: Proposal: fast-path params = {burst_tokens: 20, refill_per_sec: 2, max_consecutive_bursts: 3}. After 3 bursts in 60s, escalate to per-tenant breaker.
Noa: Agreed. Also tie to request footprint: if request triggers heavy KV/cache misses, treat it as non-fast-path.
Jules: On degrade targets: we discussed three axes: model variant (quant/distill), context-window trim, and local cache fallback. Prioritize cache, then context trim, then quant.
Priya: For context trim we should do deterministic truncation policy instead of random chop: prefer removing low-salience prefixes (system messages, old history).
Ravi M: Good call. Add a small heuristic: preserve last N turns and any system instructions.
ops-bot: note: mini-proto stored at /designs/fastpath-degrade-v1. Rolling canary planned.
Noa: Circuit semantics: per-tenant circuit state = {closed, limbo, open}. Flow: closed -> limbo on soft-fallback_threshold -> if sustained -> open and start rejecting.
Jules: What's limbo? A probation where we aggressively try degrade targets and measure quality-loss. If quality drop < threshold for X mins -> stay limbo and accept. Else open -> reject.
Priya: Add metrics emitted: tenant.circuit.state, tenant.degrade.rate, tenant.quality.delta. That helps ops decide.
Ravi M: API surface: orchestrator.admit(req) returns {decision: "PASS"|"DEGRADE"|"REJECT", fallback: "cache"|"trim"|"quant", reason_code: string, headers: [string]}. Should include estimated_cost_delta.
Noa: Important: if fallback increases latency beyond target, fallback should be aborted and we should fall back to REJECT path. So admission should include worst-case latency estimate.
Jules: Testing: add a sim harness that mixes 1000 small-tenants and 10 heavy tenants to validate fast-path fairness and circuit behaviour.
Priya: Ops playbook snippet: if global.open_count > 5 -> page infra; if any reserved-tenant in open -> immediate rollback to previous policy.
Ravi M: Action owners: Jules will draft admit proto and the fast-path token logic; Noa will add the heuristics for KV-miss classification and latency estimation; Priya will write abuse-cooldown rules + playbook; I'll update RFC + run the sim.
ops-bot: rollout plan: canary non-prod -> 5% prod -> 25% prod -> wide. See /rollouts/fastpath-degrade-2026 for details.
Noa: One last thing: log an audit event for every DEGRADE/REJECT with reason_code and tenant_id. Helps customer support.
Ravi M: Yep. I'll add that to the spec. Quick follow-up tomorrow after prototypes. :rocket:
